ai_show_review.summary: Early Dead sound at Fillmore with limited recording detail
ai_show_review.blurb: The November 18, 1966 show captures the band in its formative stage. No setlist is documented and the sole available source is of fair audio quality, offering a basic glimpse of the early Garcia/Weir interplay. It is downloadable as a 24‑bit FLAC.
ai_show_review.review: On November 18, 1966 the Grateful Dead took the stage at San Francisco’s Fillmore Auditorium during a period when their repertoire was still coalescing around blues‑rock foundations and nascent improvisational sparks. The only known recording (gd1966-11-18.169871.sbd.flegel.ciaffa.miller.flac2444) is a 24‑bit FLAC download described as “fair” in quality; reviewers provide no concrete commentary on performance, setlist flow, or standout moments. While the audio fidelity does not allow a deep dive into the band’s early dynamics, the tape remains valuable for completists interested in hearing Pigpen’s organ and harmonica contributions alongside Jerry’s nascent lead work, Bob’s steady rhythm guitar, Phil’s developing bass lines, and Bill Kreutzmann’s driving drums. Listeners should approach this release as a historical snapshot rather than a definitive musical statement.

best_recording.reason: Only known recording of the show; offers a complete, though fair‑quality, audio document for collectors.

key_highlights: Earliest documented Fillmore performance from the band's pre‑psychedelic era
Features Pigpen on keyboards and harmonica alongside the original quintet
Provides a rare audible snapshot of the group's formative sound
